startup.name: Discovered Materials
startup.one_liner: AI scientists to discover materials for the semiconductor industry.
startup.description: A swarm of AI agents to discover new materials for datacenter chips and fabs, compressing a ten year lab process to months. One founder is a Stanford PhD whose nanoscale interconnect materials entered Intel and TSMC roadmaps; the other built autonomous agents at an AI startup. Four people in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Company is assumed accepted. The prior is about 1 percent; deep technical credibility, with materials adopted into Intel and TSMC roadmaps, and an AI for science theme with large funding comps push this to the 15 percent top of the allowed range.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly decline if it could not see a near term revenue path, since materials discovery has a ten year validation cycle and chipmakers buy slowly. It would also question whether a four person team can compete with Periodic Labs and CuspAI, which raised hundreds of millions.

anchors.adjustment_reason: 1.3x the Industrials anchor: AI for science and semiconductors were drawing very large rounds in 2025 and 2026, and a founder with materials adopted by Intel and TSMC is rare; I cannot verify traction.

bands.rationale: Small round or grant funding if chip customers are slow.
Typical deep tech AI seed above the 3M US median.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed fails if investors judge that a four person team cannot match well funded labs with robotics and compute, or if the commercial story, selling materials to chipmakers, looks too far from revenue. Numerion Labs shows AI discovery companies can raise a large A and then shrink, which makes investors careful about scientific hype.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B fails if qualification cycles of five to ten years mean no revenue arrives before capital runs out, and if a materials discovered by AI cannot be manufactured economically at scale. Macromoltek (W18), a computational design shop, stayed small on grants, showing how computational discovery firms can fail to reach large rounds.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C fails if licensing revenue from materials stays small and chipmakers prefer to keep discovery in house or buy from large labs. Few computational discovery companies in the data reached C, and Atomwise's descendant Numerion Labs cut staff after a 45M A.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The long validation cycle means most failure is a stall: candidate materials without qualification, no licences, and funds that prefer better capitalised labs. A strategic sale to a chip equipment maker or materials company is the likely good exit, and Numerion Labs shows even a large Series A can end with staff cuts and a rebrand.

killers.risk: Discovered materials cannot be validated or qualified in time
killers.evidence: Materials qualification in fabs takes years and lab validation is the bottleneck the company says it will compress.
killers.mitigation: Partner with a lab or fab for validation and pick materials with short qualification paths.

killers.risk: Better funded labs win talent and customers
killers.evidence: Periodic Labs raised a 300M seed and CuspAI raised 100M, each with far larger teams.
killers.mitigation: Focus on one interconnect or thermal material and sell outcomes.

killers.risk: Revenue model is unclear and slow
killers.evidence: Chipmakers pay for materials after qualification, not for AI discovery, so early revenue may only come from pilots.
killers.mitigation: Offer paid discovery projects with design partners.

technical_complexity.rationale: AI agents proposing materials is feasible, but simulation accuracy, experimental validation and fab integration are very hard for four people. The founder's materials work gives a rare edge.

takeover_risk.rationale: Well funded labs could add semiconductor focus within two years, and suppliers could acquire talent. The incentive exists, but each has many domains to cover.

brand.rationale: A descriptive 19 character name is easy to understand but hard to own and recall, unlike short YC names such as Stripe or Airbnb; for a deep tech business sold to chipmakers it will matter little.

narrative.headline: Elite technical founders in a richly funded category, with a long road from discovery to revenue.
narrative.general_summary: Discovered Materials applies AI agents to semiconductor material discovery, led by a founder whose materials reached Intel and TSMC roadmaps. Investor appetite for AI science was very high in 2025 and 2026, which makes a seed above the YC deal likely. The risks are the long validation cycle and rivals with hundreds of millions. A Series A depends on a validated material or a paying chip partner. Analogs show AI discovery companies often stall after one large round, so the later steps stay near cohort anchors.
